title: Quantitative Disentanglement of Terahertz Spin and Orbital Pumping in 3d Ferromagnetic Heterostructures
authors: Tongyang Guan, Jiahao Liu, Yuxiao Mo, Liangliang Zhu, Yizheng Wu, Zhensheng Tao
abstract: Spin and orbital pumping - the injection of spin and orbital angular momentum from a driven ferromagnet into an adjacent nonmagnetic layer - are fundamental processes underlying angular-momentum generation and transport in magnetic heterostructures. Femtosecond optical excitation extends these phenomena into the ultrafast regime, where spintronic terahertz emission spectroscopy (STES) detects picosecond angular-momentum currents in a contact-free manner through spin-to-charge and orbital-to-charge conversion. Microscopic theory predicts that orbital-pumping efficiency increases from Fe to Ni across the 3d series, yet whether these predictions hold under ultrafast excitation remains unclear. A central challenge is that spin and orbital currents are generated simultaneously and contribute additively to the same terahertz emission, preventing their quantitative separation. Here, we overcome this limitation by combining STES with wedge-sample thickness control in heterostructures whose nonmagnetic layers (Ta, W, and Nb) have spin Hall and orbital Hall angles of opposite signs. The two angular-momentum channels therefore exhibit distinct emission polarities and thickness dependences, enabling their quantitative decomposition. Systematic measurements on Fe, Co, and Ni heterostructures reveal that the orbital-pumping contribution increases progressively toward Ni, reaching several tens of percent of the spin-current contribution - far exceeding theoretical predictions. Even Fe generates a non-negligible orbital current that becomes essential in the thin-nonmagnetic-layer regime. The extracted orbital diffusion lengths are consistently shorter than spin diffusion lengths and increase with decreasing spin-orbit coupling strength of the nonmagnetic layer. These results establish a quantitative framework for ultrafast spin and orbital pumping in magnetic heterostructures.
summary: This work quantitatively disentangles spin and orbital pumping contributions in magnetic heterostructures using ultrafast Terahertz Emission Spectroscopy (STES) combined with thickness control. By exploiting opposite THz polarities from spin and orbital currents, the authors demonstrate that orbital pumping is significantly enhanced, particularly towards Ni, exceeding current theoretical predictions. This establishes a robust, quantitative framework for studying coupled angular momentum transport in spintronic materials.
main_problem: The primary challenge is quantitatively separating the simultaneously generated and additively contributing spin and orbital angular momentum currents during ultrafast pumping in magnetic heterostructures.
main_result: The orbital pumping contribution increases significantly from Fe to Ni, reaching levels much higher than theoretical predictions, establishing a quantitative framework for ultrafast spin and orbital pumping.
method: The authors combine Spintronic Terahertz Emission Spectroscopy (STES) with wedge-sample thickness control to exploit distinct emission polarities and thickness dependencies for quantitative decomposition.
model_or_system: The study investigates FM/NM heterostructures (Fe, Co, Ni on Ta, W, Nb) using the Multi-component terahertz-emission model (MC-TEM) to analyze THz emission arising from spin-to-charge (ISHE) and orbital-to-charge (IOHE) conversions.
key_observables: THz emission polarity and amplitude as a function of nonmagnetic layer thickness ($d_{NM}$); extracted orbital ($\lambda_L$) vs. spin ($\lambda_S$) diffusion lengths; orbital-to-spin amplitude ratios ($	ilde{A}_L/	ilde{A}_S$).
important_parameters: The relative strength of orbital pumping compared to spin pumping, which increases systematically from Fe to Ni; the thickness dependence of the THz signal, revealing threshold-like behaviors.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the THz emission can be modeled as a coherent sum of bare-FM, ISHE-induced, and IOHE-induced contributions, and that the secondary orbital-to-spin conversion mechanism is not the dominant factor.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the THz emission and its decomposition (AS, AL, AFe contributions) across different FM/NM interfaces (e.g., Fe|Ta, Co|Ta, Ni|Ta) as a function of NM thickness, showing polarity reversals and thickness thresholds.
paper_structure: The paper systematically presents the experimental setup and diagnostic strategy (using opposite-signed Hall angles and thickness control) to decompose the total THz signal into its spin and orbital components, followed by quantitative analysis of the resulting pumping efficiencies and diffusion lengths.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter spintronics, the precise measurement and separation of coupled angular momentum channels (spin vs. orbital) using ultrafast spectroscopy techniques are highly relevant to understanding non-equilibrium quantum dynamics in solid-state systems.
